# docker_container_cp (Action)

Copies a file or directory into an existing container at any time, like `docker container cp SRC CONTAINER:PATH`. The source is inline `content`, `content_base64` or a local `source` path (a file or a directory, copied recursively); it is packed into a tar archive and extracted by the daemon (`PUT /containers/{id}/archive`), so the container may be running or stopped. docker_container's `files` block covers files that must exist before the first start.

Actions require Terraform 1.14 or later. An action keeps no state: it runs when
a resource's `lifecycle { action_trigger { events = [...] actions = [action.docker_container_cp.<name>] } }`
fires, or on demand with `terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_container_cp.<name>`.
Arguments go in the action's `config` block.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "docker_container" "web" {
  name  = "web"
  image = "nginx:1.27"

  lifecycle {
    action_trigger {
      events  = [after_create, after_update]
      actions = [action.docker_container_cp.index]
    }
  }
}

# Copy a page into the running container (the container may also be stopped).
#   terraform apply -invoke=action.docker_container_cp.index
action "docker_container_cp" "index" {
  config {
    container_id = docker_container.web.id
    path         = "/usr/share/nginx/html/index.html"
    content      = "<h1>deployed by Terraform</h1>"
    mode         = "0644"
    uid          = 101 # nginx
    gid          = 101
    copy_uidgid  = true # map uid / gid through a user-namespace remapping (docker cp -a)
  }
}
```

<!-- action schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `container_id` (String) The container the action targets, by ID or name, e.g. `docker_container.app.id`.
- `path` (String) Absolute destination path inside the container: the file to write, or the directory to create for a directory `source`. Its parent directory must exist.

### Optional

- `allow_overwrite_dir_with_file` (Boolean) Let a file replace an existing directory of the same name (Engine `noOverwriteDirNonDir=false`). Default `false`.
- `content` (String) Inline UTF-8 file content. Exactly one of `content`, `content_base64` and `source`.
- `content_base64` (String) Inline binary file content, base64-encoded. Exactly one of `content`, `content_base64` and `source`.
- `copy_uidgid` (Boolean) Map the archive's `uid` / `gid` through the container's user-namespace mapping so the files belong to the same user inside the container as they would without remapping (Engine `copyUIDGID`, `docker cp --archive`). Default `false`.
- `gid` (Number) Numeric group of the copied files. Default 0 (root).
- `mode` (String) Octal permission bits for the copied files, e.g. `0644` or `0755`. Default `0644` for inline content, the local file's mode for `source`.
- `result_path` (String) Local file the action writes its result object to after a successful run. The file holds one JSON object keyed by the action's output names (`result`, the identity values, the raw outputs with their `*_sha256` hashes, and the version values), with keys sorted at every level, two-space indentation and a trailing newline; it is written atomically (temporary file, then rename) and parent directories are created. Read it in a later run with `jsondecode(file(...))` or the `local_file` data source. Sensitive values are written in full, since this is your own file, but show as `(sensitive)` in the progress message. Nothing is written when the action fails.
- `source` (String) Local file or directory on the machine running Terraform; `~` expands to the home directory. Exactly one of `content`, `content_base64` and `source`.
- `uid` (Number) Numeric owner of the copied files. Default 0 (root).
